stories.headline: Centre orders rice traders to declare stocks every Friday to curb hoarding
stories.summary: The Food and Consumer Affairs Ministry says all traders, wholesalers, big chain retailers and processors holding rice or paddy must post their stocks on the Food Stock Portal every Friday. Stock limits have been approved for Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana until 31 January, and the rice target for open-market e-auctions in 2026-27 has been doubled to 50 lakh tonnes.
stories.why_it_matters: The move aims to keep rice prices in check, especially in southern states, and signals worry about food inflation.

image.alt: Workers piling harvested paddy at a grain market

impact.why: Wider stock limits and more open-market sales should ease rice prices and food inflation.
Rice exporters and millers face tighter stock rules in five southern states.

stories.headline: Election Commission gives voters left off SIR draft rolls in 7 states another chance
stories.summary: The Election Commission has opened a new window for people who filled enumeration forms but were left off the draft electoral rolls after being marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. It covers Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland. Booth Level Officers will contact them and help them apply again, including online through ECINET.

stories.headline: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal is close after meeting Putin's envoy
stories.summary: Donald Trump met Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin's special envoy, at the White House and said afterwards that the two sides are "very close" to a settlement. He says the deal could be a big agreement covering all of Europe, but gave no details. The talks follow a gathering of Russian and Ukrainian officials hosted by Melania Trump, which built on a six-day local truce that let nearly 800 civilians leave Oleshky.
stories.why_it_matters: A real peace deal could lower energy and grain prices and ease risk across global markets.
stories.note: Trump's own view; no deal terms released. The meeting is confirmed by both sources.

image.alt: Donald Trump speaking with raised hands in the Oval Office

impact.why: A Russia-Ukraine deal could ease worries about energy supply from Russia.

stories.headline: Qatar's emir urges diplomacy in Trump call as US reviews Iran's proposal
stories.summary: Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim, spoke to Trump by phone and stressed the need for diplomatic solutions to avoid further escalation. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran's nuclear proposal, sent through Qatar, is being reviewed in Washington. At sea, Iran's IRGC says two tankers hit mines on "unauthorised" routes, and UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an explosion on a tanker off Oman.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on tankers keep oil near $100 and raise India's import bill.
stories.note: US review of the proposal is per an Iranian official; IRGC mine claim not independently confirmed.

impact.why: Continued tanker attacks threaten supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Iraq's PM tells Trump Iraq will not be used to attack its neighbours
stories.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi spoke to Trump on Thursday and said Iraq will not let its land be used for attacks on neighbouring countries, his office says. Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein warned armed groups not to join any Iranian retaliation, saying new US strikes on Iran are a real possibility. Iraq has lost more than $60bn in oil revenue since the war began.

stories.headline: Strong US jobs report lifts the dollar: 165,000 jobs added in October
stories.summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than economists expected, and the jobless rate dipped to 4.1%. Hourly pay rose 0.4% in the month, and August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000 jobs. The dollar index rose about 0.6% to near 102.2 and the US 10-year yield rose to about 4.87%.
stories.why_it_matters: Solid hiring keeps a US rate hike in play, which supports the dollar and can pull money away from India.

impact.why: Hiring well above forecasts keeps the Fed hawkish.
Strong jobs and faster wage growth push Treasury yields higher.
A firmer dollar and higher yields weigh on gold.

stories.headline: Rupee closes near 93.90, its biggest one-day gain since October 12
stories.summary: The rupee closed at about 93.90 per dollar, up over 50 paise from Thursday's 94.47, after opening at 94.50 and touching 93.82. Dealers credit steady foreign buying of Indian shares and softer oil prices, while the RBI was seen buying dollars near 93.88 to slow the rise. The rupee is up about 1.2% this week.
stories.why_it_matters: A stronger rupee cuts the cost of oil imports, but RBI buying shows it does not want a sharp rise.
stories.note: PTI puts the close at 93.89 (up 52 paise); IANS at 93.91 (up 56 paise).

impact.why: Foreign inflows into Indian stocks are lifting demand for the rupee.
A firmer rupee trims export earnings of IT companies.

stories.headline: India's forex reserves fall $2.69 billion to $717.06 billion
stories.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $2.69 billion to $717.06 billion in the week to 30 October, RBI data show. Foreign currency assets dropped $2.09 billion and gold holdings fell $559 million. Reports link the fall to RBI dollar sales to support the rupee; reserves are now about $68.65 billion below their September record.

impact.why: Lower reserves leave the RBI a little less room to defend the rupee.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 1,718 points to 81,028 as rally runs to a seventh day
stories.summary: The Sensex closed up 1,718 points, or 2.2%, at 81,028 and the Nifty rose 494 points, or 2%, to 25,030, the seventh straight day of gains, even as Korea and Japan fell about 6%. Midcaps ended almost flat and smallcaps fell about 0.8%, so the rally was led by large stocks. The gains came on Dhanteras, with foreign investors buying heavily this week.
stories.why_it_matters: India is being treated as a safe place to park money while Asia's chip-heavy markets sell off.

image.alt: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai

impact.why: Heavy foreign buying is lifting large-cap Indian stocks.
Foreign money flowing into shares supports the rupee.

stories.headline: Nasdaq rebounds about 1.7% at the US open after Thursday's rout
stories.summary: US stocks opened higher after the strong jobs report, with the Nasdaq up about 1.7% and the S&P 500 up about 1% by 10:20 AM New York time, while the Dow was flat. Chip stocks bounced after Thursday's 5.5% Nasdaq plunge; in premarket trade Lam Research jumped about 11% on a $25 billion buyback and Moderna about 10% after beating forecasts.
stories.why_it_matters: A US tech rebound could calm Asian markets when they reopen on Monday.
stories.note: Levels from Yahoo Finance at 15:20 UTC; CNBC's early update showed the Dow down 1%.

impact.why: Chip and AI stocks are recovering part of Thursday's losses.
A $25 billion buyback lifted the shares.

stories.headline: Blue Origin unveils a third stage for New Glenn and a new, cheaper Northstar engine
stories.summary: Blue Origin unveiled GS3, a hydrogen-fuelled third stage that it says can send up to 20 tonnes toward the Moon or 14 tonnes straight to geostationary orbit on its biggest New Glenn version. It also revealed Northstar, a methane booster engine rated at 715,000 pounds of thrust, more than the BE-4 it would replace, with 30% less mass and half the parts. Northstar went from approval to test firings in 11 months; GS3 targets a first flight in 2028.
stories.note: Performance figures are Blue Origin's own claims.
